authority.legal_name: Norwegian county public-ferry procurement (fylkeskommune — Vestland / Møre og Romsdal / Rogaland) under the Norwegian Maritime Authority, governed by Parliament's zero-emission World Heritage fjord mandate
authority.geography_type: deep glacial fjords cutting far inland from the west coast — protected UNESCO World Heritage fjords, commuter fjord crossings, and long coastal express corridors

mandate.summary: Norway operates one of the world's most advanced public ferry systems — county-procured car ferries and express boats connecting fjord communities — and has legislated the world's most ambitious decarbonization requirement: from 2026, only zero-emission vessels may operate in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords (Nærøyfjord and Geirangerfjord). The mandate then radiates outward to the wider county ferry network. The authority's job is to keep fjord communities connected while meeting a binding zero-emission timeline.
current_priorities: Meeting the 2026 zero-emission requirement in the World Heritage fjords
Extending zero-emission operation across the county car-ferry and express-boat network
Keeping fjord and island communities reliably connected — the ferry is often the only link

policy_targets.interim_target: Norwegian Parliament: ZERO-EMISSION requirement for the UNESCO World Heritage fjords (Nærøyfjord, Geirangerfjord) from 2026 — a binding, world-first mandate; national goal to cut transport emissions in half by 2030 and climate-neutrality by 2050
policy_targets.vision: The world's greenest fjord ferry network — zero-emission in the protected fjords first, then across the whole coastal public network
policy_targets.relevance: Norway already runs the world's first battery-electric car ferry (MF Ampere, 2015) and hydrogen ferry (MF Hydra); a foiling-electric platform extends that leadership to the fast express-boat legs, where speed and range have kept diesel in service the longest — decarbonizing exactly the corridors the 2026 mandate targets.

precedent.headline: Norway already leads the world in zero-emission ferries — this is the next step, not a leap.

existing_program.operator: Norled and other county ferry operators (fylkeskommune procurement)
existing_program.program: World-first battery-electric car ferry MF Ampere (2015); hydrogen ferry MF Hydra; the all-electric 'Future of the Fjords' express vessel serving the Nærøyfjord; a national fleet of electric car ferries
existing_program.proof_stat: The 2026 zero-emission World Heritage fjord mandate is already law — the market pull exists and is binding
existing_program.note: This is a PUBLIC, county-procured network; the mandate is statutory.

interpretation_for_navier: Anchor the proposal on the UNESCO World Heritage fjord legs where zero-emission is MANDATED from 2026 (Nærøyfjord: Flåm–Gudvangen; Geirangerfjord: Geiranger–Hellesylt), then extend to the Sognefjord express and commuter crossings, then the longer coastal express corridors. Foiling-electric wins on the fast express-boat legs where range/speed kept diesel longest. Domestic-first; no cross-border link.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] — iconic fjord villages and terminals (high confidence). Precise berths and routed geometry are Grok's to seal.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The Nærøyfjord World Heritage leg — where zero-emission operation is MANDATED from 2026. The iconic protected-fjord crossing, flown clear of the water, near-silent.
The Geirangerfjord World Heritage leg — the second 2026 zero-emission-mandated fjord; the classic Geiranger–Hellesylt crossing.
The Sognefjord express line-haul from Bergen into the fjord network — a long, fast express leg where foiling range and speed replace diesel.
Inner-Sognefjord connection linking the express hub to the Nærøyfjord World Heritage gateway at Flåm.
Bergen–Askøy commuter crossing — a high-frequency urban public leg ideal for quiet zero-emission foiling.
The Lysefjord express (Pulpit Rock corridor) from Stavanger — a long fjord leg where speed and range keep diesel in service today.

regional_links.note: The proposal stands on the domestic fjord network. No cross-border corridor is minted.

routing_hazards.instruction: Route every leg down the fjord centreline in deep water to the charted village piers — never straight-line across headlands or shallow fjord arms. Provide explicit hand waypoints around fjord bends and narrows.

hazards.detail: Nærøyfjord and Geirangerfjord are strictly protected; low-wake, zero-emission foiling is the advantage, but route to charted lanes and observe protected-zone speed/wake rules.
Nærøyfjord narrows to ~250m; route the fjord centreline around bends (Bakka, Dyrdal) — never straight-line across the water.

hazards.hazard: Deep fjords, steep sides, katabatic winds
hazards.detail: Fjords funnel sudden downslope winds; weather-aware waypoints, especially on the long Sognefjord and Lysefjord legs.
Depart via charted terminal channels clear of coastal-express and cargo traffic.
Inner fjord arms can ice; long polar-winter nights require all-weather, after-dark capable operation.

sources.what: Norwegian Parliament zero-emission requirement for World Heritage fjords from 2026

MF Hydra — world's first liquid-hydrogen ferry (Norled)
Future of the Fjords — all-electric express vessel, Nærøyfjord
